conclusion: The size dichotomy cannot close, and the failure point is exact: the controlled-interval horn delivers log g(k) = o(k) if and only if max(A) = rad(S)^{o(1)}, pinned from both sides (Rankin upper, simplex-volume lower), and no optimisation over S, scale or split moves that threshold. The other horn cannot supply it, because after the only available normalisation the height of a primitive admissible set of sub-extremal size is unbounded (explicit witnesses up to 5.6e14 for k=2, |A|=3), the clique yields only a four-term S-unit relation for which no height theorem exists, and even an abc-optimal three-term bound would land at rad(S)^{1+o(1)}, one full power of the radical too high.
confidence: Lean on the threshold lemma and the height obstruction hard: both are rigorous (Rankin and the simplex volume are unconditional; the height witnesses are exhaustive enumerations re-verified by full trial division). Lean less hard on the arity paragraph, where the Evertse-Schlickewei-Schmidt and Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman bounds are cited from standard literature and were not re-derived or re-checked against sources in this run. The audit correction to r_186989 (a k=3 extremal witness with max element 475, not <50) is a direct computation and is solid.
